category.name: Find And Replace
category.preferred_workflow: Create a sample DOCX (or other supported format) in the example, load it with a Document object, configure a FindReplaceOptions instance with the appropriate flags, and invoke Document.Range.Replace using either a literal string, a Regex, or a custom IReplacingCallback; finally, save the modified document to the desired output path.

strict_api_bans: Do not reference System.Drawing; use Aspose.Drawing for any drawing-related types.
Do not assume that source files, streams, or folders exist; generate minimal sample inputs within the example code.
Do not call undocumented helpers such as Document.ReplaceAll or Paragraph.Replace.
canonical_patterns: Use Document.Range.Replace with a literal string, a Regex, or a FindReplaceOptions instance for all supported replacement scenarios.
Implement IReplacingCallback when custom replacement logic is required and assign it to FindReplaceOptions.ReplacingCallback.
When a task mentions placeholders, headers, footers, or other sections, access the corresponding Nodes collection and apply the same replace pattern.
nullable_warning_prevention: Initialize all non-nullable reference-type fields or properties before use to avoid CS8618 warnings.
Guard any value that may be null with an explicit null-check before dereferencing to prevent CS8600, CS8602, and CS8604.
Declare local variables as nullable when a null value is legitimate and handle the null case explicitly.

common_failure_patterns.symptom: The compiler reports that FindReplaceOptions does not contain definitions such as MatchWholeWord, UseRegularExpressions, or FindWholeWords.
common_failure_patterns.cause: The code references property names that were renamed or never existed in the Aspose.Words API version 26.10.0.
common_failure_patterns.fix: Use the correct property names: MatchCase for case sensitivity, FindWholeWordsOnly for whole-word matching, and rely on the Regex overload to enable regular-expression mode.
common_failure_patterns.prevention: Consult the official Aspose.Words API reference for the exact property names and avoid hard-coding undocumented members.

common_failure_patterns.symptom: Compilation fails with CS0246 because the type ReplaceEvaluator cannot be found.
common_failure_patterns.cause: The example attempts to use a non-existent delegate type instead of the documented IReplacingCallback interface.
common_failure_patterns.fix: Implement a class that inherits from IReplacingCallback and assign an instance to FindReplaceOptions.ReplacingCallback.
common_failure_patterns.prevention: Always use IReplacingCallback for custom replacement logic and verify its namespace (Aspose.Words.Replacing).

common_failure_patterns.symptom: The compiler reports CS1503 errors when a Regex and a FindReplaceOptions object are passed to an overload expecting string arguments.
common_failure_patterns.cause: The code calls the string-based Replace overload instead of the Regex overload that accepts a Regex, a replacement string, and FindReplaceOptions.
common_failure_patterns.fix: Call Document.Range.Replace with the Regex overload: Replace(Regex pattern, string replacement, FindReplaceOptions options).
common_failure_patterns.prevention: Match the argument types exactly to the overload signature; use IntelliSense or the API docs to select the correct method.

common_failure_patterns.pattern: Metacharacter replacement without real line breaks
common_failure_patterns.symptom: Runtime throws an InvalidOperationException because no replacements were made when attempting to replace multiple line-break sequences with "\n" or "&p".
common_failure_patterns.cause: The source document contains plain text literals instead of actual ControlChar.LineBreak characters, so the regex never matches.
common_failure_patterns.fix: Insert real line-break characters using ControlChar.LineBreak when building the sample document, and match them with a regex such as "(\v){2,}".
common_failure_patterns.prevention: Bootstrap the input document with the exact control characters that the replacement logic expects.

common_failure_patterns.pattern: Callback misuse leading to null parent
common_failure_patterns.symptom: Runtime throws an InvalidOperationException or ArgumentException when the callback attempts to move the DocumentBuilder to a node with a null parent.
common_failure_patterns.cause: The IReplacingCallback implementation accesses args.MatchNode without verifying that it belongs to the main story or attempts to insert breaks outside a valid paragraph.
common_failure_patterns.fix: Validate that args.MatchNode is not null and that its parent story is the main document before performing insertions; use DocumentBuilder.MoveTo(args.MatchNode) only on nodes within the main story.
common_failure_patterns.prevention: Add defensive null checks and story-type checks inside the Replacing method to ensure safe node manipulation.

narrative.overview: The Find and Replace category demonstrates how to perform literal, case-sensitive, whole-word, and regular-expression replacements in Word documents using Aspose.Words. Verified examples show correct usage of Document.Range.Replace, FindReplaceOptions, and IReplacingCallback with locally bootstrapped sample files.
narrative.purpose: Provide an AI coding assistant with clear, reproducible patterns for implementing robust find-and-replace operations in Aspose.Words, ensuring that all required namespaces are imported, documents are created or loaded locally, and only supported APIs are used.
validation_priorities: Verify that the replacement count returned by Document.Range.Replace is greater than zero; otherwise throw an informative exception.
maintenance_notes: Update the example code whenever a new Aspose.Words version changes property names or overload signatures, and run the verification suite after each upgrade.
